Subject: Review opinion on timing anomalies of a batch of meters in S-126 area

On the morning of 2026-10-22, I had a telephone discussion with the equipment engineer of a manufacturing enterprise. The other party reported that the peak electricity consumption on recent electricity bills was absurdly higher than the same period last year, but the production line shifts had not changed. I retrieved the collection data for DEV-2350, and the situation is as follows: the meter clock deviates from the master station clock by 47 minutes, and the deviation has continued to expand over the last 9 days; the battery voltage in the meter is 2.7V, already below the 3.0V undervoltage alarm threshold; the timestamps of daily frozen data are shifted forward as a whole, causing the electricity consumption from 23:00 to 24:00 each day to be counted into the previous day, exactly falling into the peak-rate period; the two rate switching points at 08:00 and 22:00 are misaligned, and peak and flat-period electricity are mixed with each other. Based on the existing data, the monthly electricity bill deviation is estimated at about ±1.8 ten-thousand yuan. The meter has been in operation for 9 years, exceeding the 8-year replacement cycle.

Conclusion: This is a clock and battery failure of the meter itself, not a characteristic of electricity theft (three-phase current balance 3.1%, no cover-opening record). Remote time synchronization can only temporarily correct the deviation, and battery undervoltage is irreversible. It is recommended to replace the meter on site and backfill the frozen data. The confidence level of the loss judgment is rated internally as "relatively high", because the electricity affected by rate-period crossover cannot be precisely split day by day.

Additionally: there are still 6 meters of the same model in batch B-14529 waiting in queue; please schedule production together. I have not yet signed the rollback plan for the system migration window; I will confirm tomorrow.
